title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 102: Statement to be annexed to notice

content.overview: Section 102 requires an explanatory statement containing material facts for each item of special business at a general meeting, including specified interests and information needed for members to understand and decide the business.
content.glance: For special business, disclose material facts and specified interests; include qualifying 2% shareholdings in another affected company, inspection details for referenced documents, and apply the amended benefit/penalty consequences. This section does not apply to an OPC: see section 122(1) and its separate procedure.
content.study:
## Material facts, interests and special business
A statement setting out material facts concerning each item of special business at a general meeting must be annexed to the notice. It must state the nature of any financial or other concern or interest of every director and the manager (if any), every other key managerial personnel, and their relatives, and include other information and facts that enable members to understand the meaning, scope and implications of the business and decide on it.

At an AGM, business is generally special except the four statutory categories of ordinary business: consideration of financial statements and the Board’s and auditors’ reports; declaration of dividend; appointment of directors in place of those retiring; and appointment of, and fixing remuneration of, auditors. At any other meeting, all business is deemed special. Where special business relates to or affects another company, the statement must also disclose the shareholding interest in that other company of each promoter, director, manager (if any) and other key managerial personnel of the first company if that interest is not less than 2% of the other company’s paid-up share capital.

## Documents, benefits and penalty
If an item refers to a document to be considered at the meeting, the statement must specify the time and place where the document can be inspected. Where non-disclosure or insufficient disclosure results in a direct or indirect benefit accruing to a promoter, director, manager, other KMP or their relatives, the relevant person holds that benefit in trust for the company and is liable to compensate the company to the extent of the benefit received. Section 102(5), as substituted by section 16 of the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019 with effect from 2 November 2018, imposes a penalty of ₹50,000 or five times the benefit accruing to the specified person or relative, whichever is higher. This is a penalty provision, not the original Act’s pre-amendment fine wording.

## Application checklist
Classify the item as ordinary or special; compare the statement against each material fact and specified interest; check the 2% related-company disclosure threshold where applicable; identify referenced documents and inspection details; and analyse benefit, compensation and penalty consequences separately. Verify the current Act, applicable rules and company-specific facts before advising.

## One Person Company limitation
Section 122(1) expressly provides that sections 98 and 100–111 do not apply to a One Person Company (OPC). Do not apply this section’s ordinary meeting mechanics to an OPC as if it were an ordinary company. Section 122(2)–(3) separately governs how ordinary business that would otherwise be transacted at an AGM is handled for an OPC. Confirm OPC status and apply the current section 122 procedure before advising.

## Private-company notification and eligibility
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs’ section 462 notification G.S.R. 464(E) dated 5 June 2015 modifies the application of sections 101–107 to private companies: the relevant provision applies unless otherwise specified in the section or the company’s articles provide otherwise. This modification is not automatic for every private company. Under G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13 June 2017, the section 462 exceptions, modifications and adaptations apply only to a private company that has not defaulted in filing its financial statements under section 137 or its annual return under section 92. Before relying on an articles-based variation, verify the company’s filing status, current notification text and articles. This is separate from the OPC disapplication under section 122(1). Source qualification: Gazette PDF copies of G.S.R. 464(E) dated 5 June 2015 and G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13 June 2017 were retrieved through IndiaCode. Their operative text supports the section 101–107 table entry and the section 92/137 filing-default eligibility condition. The IndiaCode-hosted Gazette PDF copy of corrigendum S.O. 2218(E), dated 13 July 2017, has now been retrieved and inspected. It corrects “statement or” to “statement and” in paragraph 5, table item (ii), of G.S.R. 583(E); on the text inspected, that correction concerns the section 143(3)(i) auditor-reporting exemption and does not amend the section 101–107 table row or paragraph 2A filing-default eligibility condition. The direct MCA-hosted PDFs and later/current notification position remain to be independently checked; this is not final legal sign-off. This is not final legal sign-off.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 102: Statement to be annexed to notice

examples.title: Disclosure of related-company interest
examples.body: A proposed special-business item affects another company. A promoter or KMP of the first company holds 3% of the other company’s paid-up share capital. The explanatory statement must disclose that interest because it meets the section 102(2) proviso’s 2% threshold.

examples.title: Statement attached but disclosure incomplete
examples.body: The notice includes an explanatory statement but omits a specified interest, a qualifying related-company shareholding, or inspection details for a document to be considered. Attaching a document alone does not establish compliance.

hypotheticals.question: A company’s EGM notice includes special business affecting another company. A KMP of the first company holds 2.5% of the other company’s paid-up share capital, and the statement omits that interest. The notice also refers to a report to be considered but gives no inspection details. What are the issues?
hypotheticals.analysis: All EGM business is special. Under the proviso to section 102(2), a 2.5% holding crosses the not-less-than-2% threshold and must be disclosed for the specified persons. Under section 102(3), the statement must specify when and where the referenced document may be inspected. Counsel should assess the complete facts, any resulting benefit under section 102(4), and the current section 102(5) penalty, as amended in 2019.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What must an explanatory statement under section 102 contain, and what follows from inadequate disclosure?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: An explanatory statement must set out material facts for each item of special business, specified interests of directors/manager/KMP and relatives, other facts needed for an informed decision, qualifying 2% shareholding interests in another company affected by the business, and inspection details for referenced documents. A benefit from non-disclosure or insufficient disclosure may be held in trust for the company with compensation liability; section 102(5), as amended in 2019, provides a penalty of ₹50,000 or five times the benefit, whichever is higher.
